comments.author: jaykrown
comments.body:
I'm interested in this game idea, how far are you going to go with it? And what's your idea for combat and game progression? Here's a screenshot of the bug I experienced when trying to animate:

https://preview.redd.it/uadn99ixx6nh1.jpeg?width=542&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=218bc8f7da3f4c64b280dd345baff985accfe4f9

replies.author: cody-fifth-door
replies.body: Well it's more of an asset creation tool for a variety of games! One that I'm working on is a tower defense game like those old WC3 games.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body:
I appreciate your reply. I have an eye for gamifying things that may not make sense until built. What I'm wondering was if you were ever considering gamifying this idea in anyway? What model are you using to generate and animate? If you'd want to discuss and potentially work on an idea to make it monetizable I'm happy to talk about it. Basically, what I'm saying is this idea you had to create this, you are in my opinion about half way to something that could become a really good gameplay loop to bring users back and pay money.

I'm currently working on a game called Slingshot Speeders, which is the first orbital racing game, if you're interested in my experience.

replies.author: deeplywoven
replies.body: It would be good to allow the walking animations to walk purely sideways instead of at an angle towards the camera, that they could work with 2d metrooidvanias and sidescrolling platformers.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Maybe, that is the right type of thinking, but I wonder, the thing that gives these kinds of unique characters value is that players can see each other's characters.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: To be honest, knowing what I know about architectural design, it doesn't seem like you have the framework capable of building that level of complexity given the bugs I've experienced. I just tried to animate another character, it said "the walk is hers now" yet nothing appeared. Always ensure there is error feedback for the user when something doesn't work properly.

replies.author: cody-fifth-door
replies.body: Oh this is something I just threw up, one of a couple different projects I'm working on! I appreciate the feedback though!

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: I wish you the best, continuing to be completely honest, I'm highly tempted to rebuild what you've created in pure rust and web assembly to make something insanely rapid and efficient. If you're ever interested in collaborating let me know, I think a game like that would require to people working on a shared project.
